description: Cases for a plugin bundle's manifest (phase 5 no-terminal amendment, 4.4), run by @lushly-dev/loam-manifest's read-plugin.test.ts and meant for loam-desktop's Rust inspect (step 9c). Each case is `base` with its `patch` applied as an RFC 7386 JSON merge patch (null removes a key; an array is replaced whole). `refused` lists every refusal by code and key, in no order; `appCases` add each app's packed manifest, as much of it as the rules read. `bundleDigest` is the amendment's 7.1 digest of a bundle's files, each given by its path and its bytes' SHA-256, computed apart from either implementation. `archives` holds the `.loam-plugin` archive cases (step 9a2), described in its own `description`.

archives.description: Cases for a `.loam-plugin` archive (phase 5 no-terminal amendment, 4.4's archive rules; step 9a2), run by @lushly-dev/loam-cli's plugin-archive.test.ts and meant for loam-desktop's Rust inspect (step 9c), which must accept each valid case and refuse each refused one with the same code and the same `reason`. An archive is read only in the one canonical form `loam plugin pack` writes, and each refused case deviates from it in one field (or, under its name, in several, to pin the order in which faults are reported). A case's archive is built byte for byte, and `sha256` is the SHA-256 of its bytes, which `node scripts/archive-cases.mjs` in @lushly-dev/loam-manifest (Node.js alone, no package; `--write` sets them) builds apart from loam-cli's zip-test-support.ts and checks, and which a manifest test runs. Its entries are its base's (`base`, a pure-app bundle, unless the case says `"base": "engine"`, `engineBase`, a mounted app and its engine), less any in `remove`, with `set`'s fields set on the base entry of each path it names; then the case's `entries`; then for `repeat` `count` entries named by `path` with `{n}` from 0 and its other fields; `all`'s fields are set on every one. They are written in increasing order of the name's UTF-8 bytes unless `archive.unsorted`, after the archive's `prefixHex`: each entry's `gapHex`, its local header, its name, its local extra field, its body and, for `descriptor`, a data descriptor; then the archive's `beforeDirectoryHex`; then the central directory, one entry each in the same order; then the end record, its comment and `trailingHex`. An entry's name is `path` as UTF-8, or `nameHex`; its data `text` as UTF-8, `zeros` bytes of zero, or `hex`. It is deflated (method 8) unless `method` says otherwise, its body `bodyHex`, the raw deflate bytes given, so every builder writes the same ones; any other method's body is the data itself. Every field is little-endian and canonical unless the entry sets it. The local header: signature 0x04034b50; version needed `versionNeeded` (20); flags `flags` (0x0800, the name is UTF-8; bit 3 added by `descriptor`); method; time `time` (0); date `date` (0x0021, 1980-01-01); the CRC-32 (`crc`, else the data's), compressed size (`compressed`, else the body's length) and uncompressed size (`declared`, else the data's length), all 0 with `descriptor`; name length; extra length. `local` overrides the local header's `path`, `versionNeeded`, `flags`, `method`, `time`, `date`, `crc`, `compressed`, `declared` and `extraHex`. With `descriptor`, the body is followed by the signature 0x08074b50 (left out when `descriptor` is `unsigned`), the CRC-32 (`descriptorCrc`, else the entry's), the compressed size and the uncompressed size. A central entry: signature 0x02014b50; version made by, `madeBy` (3) shifted left 8 OR'd with `madeByVersion` (20); version needed; flags; method; time; date; the CRC-32 and both sizes; name length; extra length (of `extraHex`); comment length (of `commentHex`); disk `disk` (0); internal attributes `internal` (0); external attributes, the Unix `mode` in octal (`100644`, or `100755` with `executable`) shifted left 16 plus `dosAttributes` (0); and the local header's offset (`localOffset`, else where its record was written); then the name, `extraHex` and `commentHex`. The end record: signature 0x06054b50; `disk` and `directoryDisk` (0); the entry count on this disk (`countHere`, else `count`) and in all (`count`, else the entries'); the central directory's size plus `sizeDelta`; its offset (`offset`, else where it was written); the comment's length; then the comment, `commentHex` followed by `commentZeros` zero bytes. `refusals` lists each refusal by code, key and `reason`: `(archive)` names the archive as a whole, and any other key an entry's name or a bundle file. `reason` is the rule the refusal names, one stable tag each, which 9c must give too: of the structure, end-record, comment, signature-in-end-record, zip64, disk, entry-counts, directory-size, name-encoding, name-empty, name-order, made-by, version-needed, flags, stored, method, time-date, extra-field, internal-attributes, mode, not-regular, tiling, local-header, signature-in-directory; of the bounds, too-many-entries, declared-size, archive-size; of the data, stream-unfinished, stream-corrupt, stream-too-long, stream-trailing, size-crc; of the names, path, fold, file-in-file, duplicate; of what it holds, manifest-missing, staging, bundle (any of the directory bundle's own rules), mode-engine, mode-executable; and archive-file for a file that is not a regular one or changed while read. With more than one fault, the one reported is the first in this order (4.4's archive rules): the structure, then the bounds, then the data, then the names, then what the archive holds.
